tasks.summary: Match the Bing API account and website scope before reading search or crawl data.
tasks.context: Bing reporting begins with a verified website. If the wrong account is connected, the API can work while the intended website is absent from the returned inventory.
steps: Open the Bing Webmaster connection and inspect the available verified sites.
Compare the exact site URL with the website you want to investigate.
If the site is absent, check its verification and permissions in the connected Bing account.
Open the intended site and refresh before interpreting its report.
tasks.verify: The selected site should match the verified website in Bing Webmaster Tools, including the relevant hostname.
tasks.caution: Do not create duplicate website properties solely to fix a mobile list. Check account ownership and verification first.

tasks.title: Read Bing search and crawl reports in context
tasks.summary: Separate Bing’s search observations from Google visibility and on-site analytics.
tasks.context: Different search engines crawl and report independently. A change in a Bing report should be investigated using Bing’s website context rather than assuming Google reports must show the same result.
steps: Select the intended Bing-verified website in Verceltics.
Inspect the available search and crawl information, noting any reporting window or status context.
Compare the observed issue with the public page and the same site in Bing Webmaster Tools.
Use the provider’s supported tooling for any indexing or crawl action outside the mobile report.
tasks.verify: Report the search engine, website and observed state explicitly, especially when comparing provider reports.
tasks.caution: A public page being reachable does not prove Bing has indexed it. Report freshness and available dimensions can differ between providers.

overview: Microsoft Clarity is a behavioral-insights connection, separate from traffic counters and search visibility reports. Verceltics reads the project’s export data rather than replaying every Clarity dashboard capability in a native app.

The app’s connection guidance specifies a project export token and a recent three-day export context. That makes the integration useful for recent behavioral summaries, while long-term analysis and session replay remain questions for Clarity’s own supported tools.
capabilities: Connect a named Clarity project using its export token.
Inspect available recent behavioral, session and interaction summaries.
Keep project identity and export reporting limits visible.
setup: Open the intended Clarity project and obtain its export token from the Data Export settings.
Choose Microsoft Clarity under Sites and enter a recognizable project name and the export token.
Optionally add the public HTTPS site URL for context, keeping the credential tied to the actual Clarity project.
Connect and inspect the recent export data, remembering the app’s documented three-day export context.
troubleshooting: Clarity export tokens belong to a project. Check that the token and project label refer to the same website.
A short export window should not be interpreted as a complete historical or session-replay archive.
limit: Available metrics and history follow Clarity’s export API. The native connection does not promise session replay, full dashboard parity or arbitrary long-term reporting.

tasks.title: Understand the Clarity project export window
tasks.summary: Use recent Clarity export data without presenting it as an unlimited behavior history.
tasks.context: Clarity’s native connection is based on project export data. The app documents a recent three-day context, so the visible summary must be interpreted within that export scope.
steps: Select the Clarity project whose export token you configured.
Inspect the recent session and behavioral summaries returned for that connection.
Confirm the project and available reporting context before comparing with a screenshot from the Clarity dashboard.
Use Clarity itself when the investigation needs older history or a capability outside the export report.
tasks.verify: Your summary should state that it concerns the returned recent export data for the selected project.
tasks.caution: Do not describe an absent older period as deleted data. A short export is not evidence about every historical Clarity session.

tasks.title: Compare Clarity behavior insights with traffic reports
tasks.summary: Use interaction summaries to complement, rather than replace, visitor and acquisition metrics.
tasks.context: A traffic increase says little about how visitors interact with a page. Clarity can add behavioral context, while another provider’s visitors or sessions remain a separate measurement.
steps: Open the relevant Clarity project and read the behavioral or interaction signals exposed by its export report.
Compare the timing with the traffic change in the appropriate analytics provider, keeping the reporting windows explicit.
Identify a page or interaction question to investigate in Clarity’s own tools when more detail is needed.
Record a focused observation without merging incompatible session or visitor totals.
tasks.verify: A useful conclusion distinguishes the traffic observation from the behavioral evidence that supports a follow-up.
tasks.caution: Verceltics does not stitch individual users across providers or provide live account actions through the Discord helper. Avoid inferring a causal explanation from one summary metric.

overview: Plausible provides privacy-focused website analytics through a Stats API connection. Verceltics uses the exact site ID and API key to read a specific website’s visitors, visits, page views and engagement reporting.

The site ID is an analytics identifier, not an arbitrary display label. A domain alias or a URL with an added scheme can be different from the site ID configured in Plausible, so matching the provider’s identifier is a useful first troubleshooting step.
capabilities: Read the selected Plausible site’s supported traffic and engagement reports.
Inspect visitors, visits and page views without combining other analytics providers.
Keep the exact Plausible site identity tied to its Stats API access.
setup: Create a Stats API key in Plausible account settings with access to the intended site.
Copy the exact Site ID used by the Plausible dashboard rather than inventing a local website label.
Choose Plausible under Sites and enter that Site ID and Stats API key.
Connect and compare the site and reporting window with the same property in Plausible.
troubleshooting: A Site ID mismatch can fail even when the API key is valid. Compare the exact configured identifier.
API access and the available report scope depend on the Plausible account and service configuration.
limit: Supported API access follows Plausible’s account and deployment configuration. Use only hosting and endpoint options exposed by your installed app; the connection is not permission to send keys to an arbitrary analytics host.

tasks.title: Fix a Plausible Site ID mismatch
tasks.summary: Compare the exact provider identifier before changing a working Stats API key.
tasks.context: The analytics property is selected by its Site ID. A hostname that looks right in a browser address bar is not automatically the exact identifier expected by the Stats API.
steps: Open the intended site in Plausible and identify its configured Site ID.
Compare it character-for-character with the value entered in Verceltics, including any domain variation.
Verify that the Stats API key can access that site under the connected Plausible account.
Retry the site report and compare an equivalent reporting window.
tasks.verify: The mobile report should identify the same Plausible site you selected in the provider dashboard.
tasks.caution: Do not broaden key access or change the website’s analytics identifier as the first response to a typo. Preserve provider restrictions.

tasks.title: Read Plausible visitors, visits and page views
tasks.summary: Use each metric’s meaning and the same site period when reviewing traffic.
tasks.context: Visitors, visits and page views describe different units of activity. Their relationship can help explain a traffic change, but one metric should not be renamed as another for comparison with a different provider.
steps: Select the Plausible site and note the report period in the available view.
Read visitors, visits and page views together with the supported engagement details.
Check relevant breakdowns in the same report context to narrow the change.
Compare the same site and window in Plausible if the numbers appear inconsistent.
tasks.verify: A report should preserve the metric names and period, rather than presenting every count as unique people.
tasks.caution: Plausible and another analytics service can measure different populations. Do not sum their totals or assume a difference proves that one provider is wrong.

overview: Umami can run as a cloud service or on your own HTTPS host. Verceltics makes that hosting choice explicit because a Cloud API key and a self-hosted bearer token are different authentication contracts.

The documented native flow reads website traffic over a 30-day context. Keep the website identity, host and authentication mode together when comparing results, especially if you maintain both a production analytics instance and a development instance.
capabilities: Choose Umami Cloud or a self-hosted HTTPS instance explicitly.
Browse accessible websites and supported traffic reports.
Inspect the documented 30-day traffic context without merging other analytics providers.
fields: Umami Cloud API key, or a self-hosted bearer token
HTTPS base URL for self-hosted mode
setup: Decide whether the website is tracked by Umami Cloud or your own Umami instance.
For Cloud, obtain the Cloud API key. For self-hosted mode, prepare the intended instance’s HTTPS base URL and a bearer token for that instance.
Choose Umami under Sites, select the matching hosting mode and enter the matching credential. Enter the base URL only for the intended self-hosted service.
Connect and verify the website inventory and report context against that same Umami instance.
troubleshooting: A Cloud API key is not a substitute for a self-hosted bearer token. Check the hosting-mode selection.
A self-hosted URL must be HTTPS and point to the intended instance; a different instance can legitimately contain a different website list.
limit: Self-hosted API behavior depends on the installed Umami version and configuration. A Cloud connection and a self-hosted connection are separate accounts, not a combined analytics history.

tasks.title: Choose Umami Cloud or self-hosted authentication
tasks.summary: Match the hosting mode, credential type and HTTPS endpoint before connecting.
tasks.context: Many Umami connection failures are mismatches between deployment mode and credential. Cloud and self-hosted instances should be treated as distinct services with their own website inventories.
steps: Identify which Umami service actually tracks the production website.
Select Cloud or Self-hosted in the Verceltics connection form to match that service.
Use the Cloud API key for Cloud, or the intended HTTPS instance URL and bearer token for self-hosted mode.
Verify a known website appears before reading its traffic report.
tasks.verify: The connection should return websites from the expected instance and account, not just accept a plausible-looking URL.
tasks.caution: Never send a token to a host you have not verified. Changing from Cloud to self-hosted mode does not migrate historical analytics data.

tasks.title: Review Umami website traffic in its report window
tasks.summary: Keep website identity and the documented 30-day context consistent when comparing activity.
tasks.context: Traffic belongs to a website record within a specific Umami instance. A site with the same display name elsewhere may have a different identifier and a different history.
steps: Open the connected Umami service and choose the website associated with the production domain.
Read the available traffic report and its 30-day context documented for the native integration.
Compare the website identifier and period with the same instance’s own reporting.
Refresh after a known tracking change and distinguish current collection from previously stored activity.
tasks.verify: Your comparison should name the Umami instance, website and reporting context.
tasks.caution: Do not interpret a new instance’s empty history as data loss on the old one. The mobile connection does not consolidate data across instances.

overview: UptimeRobot monitors website or service availability from its own monitoring infrastructure. Verceltics reads monitor state, uptime ratios and response-time information through a read-only connection in the Sites workspace.

An uptime monitor and an application’s internal health checks can observe different failures. Treat the monitor’s target, returned state and measurement period as part of the evidence rather than assuming one green status proves every user journey works.
capabilities: Browse accessible UptimeRobot monitors through a read-only key.
Inspect monitor state, uptime ratios and response-time information.
Use monitor observations alongside hosting and DNS context during an incident.
setup: Create a read-only key in UptimeRobot’s Integrations & API area for the account or monitors you intend to inspect.
Choose UptimeRobot under Sites and enter the read-only key.
Verify that the expected monitor and target appear in the inventory.
Open its state, uptime and response-time details and compare the reporting context with UptimeRobot.
troubleshooting: An account-scoped and a monitor-scoped key can expose different inventories. Verify the intended scope.
A monitor can be healthy while a different hostname, route or authenticated workflow fails. Compare the target.
limit: The documented connection is for read-only monitoring. Verceltics does not create an independent uptime network or guarantee service availability.

tasks.title: Read UptimeRobot state and response time
tasks.summary: Identify the monitor target and reporting context before interpreting an incident.
tasks.context: Response time is a measurement of a particular monitor check. It is not the same as a browser’s page-load time or a complete application performance trace. A monitor aimed at the homepage can pass while an API route or signed-in workflow fails, so compare the configured target with the exact URL users report as broken.
steps: Select the UptimeRobot connection and find the monitor for the affected website or service.
Confirm its target and current state before reading the available response-time information.
Compare the timing with a public service check and the corresponding hosting deployment.
Refresh and preserve the specific monitor observation when reporting the issue.
tasks.verify: Your report should identify which target was monitored and what UptimeRobot observed.
tasks.caution: A response-time improvement does not prove that frontend rendering improved. Monitoring checks and real user experience measure different aspects of a service.

tasks.title: Interpret UptimeRobot uptime ratios
tasks.summary: Keep the monitoring period and target consistent when comparing availability.
tasks.context: An uptime percentage is meaningful only with its target and measurement period. A current healthy state can coexist with a lower historical uptime ratio after a recent incident.
steps: Open the intended monitor and read its current state separately from historical uptime ratios.
Note the reporting windows available in the returned monitor details.
Compare like periods for the same target instead of averaging percentages from unrelated monitors.
Use the provider’s incident history or supported details to investigate a change in the ratio.
tasks.verify: Describe current state and historical availability as separate observations.
tasks.caution: Do not average uptime percentages to invent an account-wide SLA. The read-only connection does not alter monitor settings or resolve the underlying outage.

overview: Better Stack’s Uptime API exposes monitors and their availability context. Verceltics uses a Uptime API token to bring that monitor inventory, check cadence and current state into a separate native Sites connection.

This integration concerns Uptime resources. Better Stack also offers other products, but an Uptime connection should not be assumed to grant access to every log, telemetry, incident-management or billing capability in the broader platform.
capabilities: Read accessible Better Stack Uptime monitors.
Inspect monitor state, check cadence and availability information.
Relate monitor observations to hosting, domain and DNS checks without merging data.
setup: Create a Uptime API token for the intended Better Stack account and monitor resources.
Choose Better Stack under Sites and enter the token in the protected connection form.
Confirm a known monitor and its target appear in the returned inventory.
Review state and check cadence, then compare with the same Uptime monitor in Better Stack.
troubleshooting: An API token for another Better Stack product may not authorize the Uptime monitor endpoint.
A missing monitor can reflect the wrong account or token scope rather than a deleted service.
limit: The documented integration reads Uptime monitor resources. It is not a promise of full Better Stack product parity or an automatic incident-resolution service.

tasks.title: Read Better Stack monitor cadence and state
tasks.summary: Understand what a monitor checks and how often before judging detection freshness.
tasks.context: A monitor’s last observed state reflects its configured check cadence and provider reporting. An application change may occur between checks, so compare timestamps and the target before calling a result stale.
steps: Open the Better Stack Uptime connection and select the relevant monitor.
Confirm the monitored target and read the returned state.
Inspect check cadence and any available timing context, keeping them separate from application request latency.
Refresh and compare with the provider’s monitor view if an incident and the displayed state appear inconsistent.
tasks.verify: A useful observation states the target, provider-returned state and relevant check cadence.
tasks.caution: Changing a check interval can affect monitoring behavior and plan usage. This guide concerns reading the configured state, not silently changing it.

tasks.title: Check Better Stack Uptime token scope
tasks.summary: Identify the right API product and account when monitors do not appear.
tasks.context: Better Stack has more than one product surface. A credential intended for another service is not proof of authorization to list Uptime monitors.
steps: Confirm that the token was created for Better Stack Uptime and the intended account.
Compare its resource scope with the monitor you expect to inspect.
Reconnect using the correct token through the Better Stack Sites connection and read the inventory.
Verify a known target before interpreting an empty monitor list as a production problem.
tasks.verify: A successful inventory check should return a monitor from the expected Uptime account.
tasks.caution: Do not send unrelated logging credentials to an Uptime endpoint or broaden all account permissions to troubleshoot one missing monitor.
